_note: Standing Ledger meanings for operator pages (source of truth for the canvas-ledger skill). tv_scan_cli.py page pulls entries from here; pages add only their own new codes. plain_headers need no Ledger row. free_text_headers are not scanned for coded values (tickers, industries, reasons). letter_coded_headers maps a column to its allowed letters; each cell is explained by the field row plus one row per letter.

entries.meaning: Letters written in order F C P D T, only the ones that are on. Example FCPD means F, C, P, and D are on and T is off. - means none of the five are on.
On: pack forming sleeve, or weeks early ≥ 0.4 with rng under 55. Off: neither.
On: earnings dte ≤ 45. Off: no print inside 45 days, or dte missing.
On: 25-week Δbo ≥ 0.15 and at least 8 weeks in the span. Off: breakout flat, down, or too few weeks.
On: setup Peer is DISCOUNT (val_vs_ind ≤ −5). Off: PREMIUM, INLINE, THIN, NA, or no peer. pe_peer and pe_fwd_peer do not turn D on.
On: tech_sma is ABOVE and rng < 85. Off: below the 50-day, or range already paid.
Count of letters in Mesh (0–5). Mesh 3+ is the filter nmesh ≥ 3.
Operating margin, %. Quality of the current business. Not a score.
Trailing TradingView PE (pe), projection forward PE (pe_fwd / fp_pe_y1), PE versus growth. pe_fwd_tv stays empty. pe_fwd is a derivative and can be off.
Model terminal price, model upside %, own-lane revenue CAGR. Separate from street and pack.
Unused upside %, max(street PT / close − 1, edge forward upside). Not mix.
Street target versus close, %. Separate from left.
leftover_carrier: street_left < 0 and left > 0. Pack leftover is the edge number. The street target is below the price.
leftover_carrier: street_left > 0 and left is above it. Edge lifted the pack number.
leftover_carrier: street_left > 0 and left is not above it.
leftover_carrier: left is missing or not positive, or street_left is missing.
Analyst PT in dollars, or close × (1 + street leftover %).
Pack leftover in dollars: close × (1 + leftover %). Edge leftover can sit above street.
leftover / max(52w range used, 15). High = unused upside vs already-paid range. Not a 0–100 score.
discount_momentum or premium_strength. Empty means the name is off the ten-name payoff focus.
Quoted multiple at least 5% cheaper than the industry median (val_vs_ind ≤ −5), and weeks bo at least 0.15.
Quoted multiple at least 5% richer (val_vs_ind ≥ 5), and weeks bo at least 0.5.
Upside from entry_high to the value target, divided by the distance down to exit_stop. The order of the ten. Not rr and not a 0–100.

value when year-1 inline upside is positive. value_below when that price is already under the band, so street does not take over. discount when year-1 is missing and the quoted inline price is above the band. street only when neither value price was computed.
Year-1 PE capitalized at the industry median forward PE. The only horizon priced.
value_y1_px when that PE is usable. Otherwise trailing PE, then EV/EBIT, then EV/Rev. EBITDA is not used.
The other peer price. EV/EBIT when that multiple and its median are on the row. Otherwise EV/Rev. Not EV/EBITDA.
evebit or evrev. missing when neither is on the row.
pe_y1, pe_trail, evebit, evrev, or missing.
above_oldest, below_oldest, at_oldest, or unknown, versus close_first / oldest_close when that column is on the row. Not a sort key.
Percent from that oldest close to today's close.
Percent from entry_high up to exit_target.
Percent from entry_high down to exit_stop. Negative.
Dollars that earn $1,000 if exit_target prints. 10% upside is $10,000. 50% upside is $2,000.
Dollar profit on a $10,000 check at up_from_entry_pct. 10% upside is $1,000.
Dollar profit on a $5,000 check at up_from_entry_pct. 50% upside is $2,500.
The buy band. Above the 50-day it runs from the average to the close. Under it, it starts at the 50-day.
First trim. The 50-day when trim_state is trim_at_sma. Empty when through_average. Not the kill.

trim_at_sma: close is above the 50-day and trim_px is that average. through_average: close is already under the 50-day, so the trim has printed and trim_px is empty. at_average: close is on the average. unknown: the 50-day gap is missing.
Price under the band that ends this entry. 1.5 times ATR under the band.
Same price as exit_stop. A print there ends this entry. kill_scope is this_entry. On an entry-book row the width is 1.5 ATR. On a timing-policy row the width is kill_atr_units (0.75 or 1.0).
ATR multiple under the band that produced kill_px. 1.5 on the entry book. 0.75 or 1.0 on the timing policy.
Recent high times 0.90. The price where the 10% drawdown leg turns on or off.
in_drawdown: close is at or under thesis_drawdown_px. above_drawdown: close is above it. unknown: the high is missing.
Prior close times 1.05. A print there is a 5% day.
through_chase: close is at or above thesis_chase_px. under_chase: close is below it. unknown: no price.
prior_close, session_open (backed out of the day's percent), or this_close when the day percent is missing.
downside_atr_units times ATRP. The timing-levels file uses 1.5. Not the timing kill.
street_up_pct divided by downside_atr_pct. The order key of the low-downside screen. Not a 0–100.
15% under average cost when cost is on the row. Book thesis-kill zone. Separate from kill_px.
Street price when the row has one. Separate from the pack leftover price.
Reading order inside the ten. Not a Daily rank.
Position in the 52-week range, 0–100. High (~85+) = paid. Low = unused range.
Relative strength index, 0–100.
Weeks breakout_long_v1 score. Δbo = change vs the prior pred run.
Weeks quality_continuation_v1.
Weeks forward_edge_active_v2.
Close vs the 50-day average, %. Required next to ABOVE / BELOW.
Close vs the 200-day average, %. Required next to the 200-day ABOVE / BELOW label.
5-day / 1-month / session price return, %.
Week return (Perf.W).
3-month return (Perf.3M). Dedicated MOVERS (3M) suite, not the DAILY Tape section.
Relative volume vs 10-day average.
Calendar days until next earnings (from the all-fields day folder).
manager_action_signal (e.g. add_long_breakout, avoid_value_trap). Not operator conviction.
Market-timing-policy action: ENTER_SMALL / ENTER_PROBE / WATCH / AVOID_CHASE. Climate, not a buy list.
Pack suggested_conviction 0.15–0.90 for a named course. Not a probability.
Operator High / Med / Low after reading conflicts.
How many pack sleeves confirm the name (unpaid, continuation, forming, …).
Enterprise value / trailing revenue.
Trailing price / earnings.
Projection forward PE (fp_pe_y1). A derivative. Can be off. pe_fwd_tv is the empty TradingView forward PE.
PE / earnings growth.
Enterprise value / trailing EBITDA.
% vs industry median multiple. Negative = cheaper (discount). Peer set is US $2B industry, min n=6.
Leftover or 5D vs industry median. Positive leftover = more unused upside than peers.
Tape column: pack val_label + val (generic_utils.setup). Not always EV/Rev.
Tape column: the bin on the one multiple setup quoted (val_field). Always show val_vs_ind beside it. Not a substitute for the trailing TV bins or the forward bins.
Percent versus the industry median of val_field. Negative = cheaper. The peer label uses this column.
The industry median of val_field.
Percent versus the industry average of val_field. A different column from val_vs_ind. It does not change DISCOUNT / PREMIUM / INLINE.
The industry average of val_field.
Percent versus the industry median, and versus the industry average, of the efficiency field. Two columns.
Same pair for each relative metric (pe, pe_fwd, peg, evrev, evebitda, pb, evfcf, opm, left, d5, and the rest on the row). Median percent and average percent stay separate.
Tape column: leftover + weeks bo / cont / fwd.
Tape column: tech_sma plus vs50, and tech_rng plus rng. RSI and ADX stay separate.
Up-tape: leftover / weeks / Val-Peer still justify the print.
Up-tape: paid range, leftover gone, premium vs peers. Do not add.
Up-tape: price moved without leftover / weeks / value support.
Neither clean case (up or down). Canvas may omit down-MIXED.
Down-tape: leftover / unused range / cheap vs industry / live profile can justify a bounce.
Down-tape: limited leftover + deterioration — likely to keep falling.
Pack/CLI field on movers laggards: BOUNCE / CONTINUE_DOWN / MIXED.
That column's percent versus the industry median is ≤ −5. At least 5% cheaper.
That column's percent versus the industry median is ≥ 5. At least 5% richer.
That column's percent is between −5 and 5. Close to the median.
DISCOUNT / PREMIUM / INLINE / THIN / NA on TradingView trailing PE (pe), taken as published. The percent beside it is pe_vs_ind.
Same bins on TradingView trailing EV/EBITDA (evebitda). The percent is evebitda_vs_ind.
Same bins on TradingView price/book and EV/FCF. Percents are pb_vs_ind and evfcf_vs_ind.
Same bins on the projection forward PE (pe_fwd). The percent is pe_fwd_vs_ind. Derivative. Can be off. Not the same word as pe_peer.
Same bins on the projection forward EV/EBITDA (evebitda_fwd). The percent is evebitda_fwd_vs_ind. Derivative. Can be off.
Peer skipped: industry n < 6, or no quoteable multiple (ETF, missing native field). No percent.
Multiple generic_utils.setup chose to quote. Not EV/Rev unless val_field is evrev.
tech_sma: close versus the 50-day average. ABOVE is vs50 ≥ 0. BELOW is vs50 < 0. The percent is vs50. tech_sma200 uses vs200 the same way.
tech_rng. UNUSED is rng under 40. PAID is rng at least 85. MID is between. The position is rng.
50-day simple moving average. If vs50 > 0, first stop below. If vs50 < 0, bounce above — stop is ATR or c15.
Nearest structure print still under today's close (SMA50, ATR, or c15).
First→last all-fields span (close / EV/Rev / street PT / ATRP). Not a 0–100.
First→last % change in close and street PT from series_span. Older notes say pt_chg for the same PT change.
All-fields span: price did not consume the target (close_pct ≤ 5 and pt_pct ≥ −2, with pack leftover still live).
All-fields span: price ran and the target did not (close_pct ≥ 8 and pt_pct ≤ 2). Rank these below ASYM.
That name's own val_field fell on the span (val_pct < −5). Not EV/Rev unless val_field is evrev.
Span has fewer than 8 all-fields days. Not a rank.
Order, not a 0–100. Payoff shortlist that is OPENING or CHEAPER, sorted by rr, tie-break bo.
Same survivors sorted by weeks bo. A second order. Do not add it to rr.
Risk-adjusted score (weeks / months).
Portfolio net asset value = equity mark + cash (capital.nav_usd).
Cost-basis weight of invested USD. Excludes cash. Not risk weight.
Name as % of NAV. Ceiling if the position goes to zero.
Further drop from **today's mark** (USD and % NAV).
Price 15% below **cost** (continuity thesis-kill zone).
Average True Range ($ / %). Structure stop uses 1.5× ATRP.
If every Book name is −10% from here, NAV change.
US-listed names with market cap ≥ $2B (pack universe).
Currently held. New = not held.
Open a line not held today. Starter about $5,000. Daily budget 0–2. Not on edge_only.
Add to a held line. About $1,000, toward the 50-day, above atr_stop, leftover live, mix not avoid. Daily budget 0–2.
Keep the line as sized. No new dollars.
Keep the line, do not add. Default for avoid_value_trap on a live-leftover Book line. Does not silently become HOLD.
Sell part of the line (trim33 / trim50). Locks a win or de-risks size. Sticks until weeks RAS ≥ 0.25 and SMA50 held.
Sell the whole line. A prior ADD/NEW cannot become EXIT unless thesis_kill. Stays EXIT until tape repairs.
Named candidate, not filled. Waits for the band, the 50-day reclaim, or the print.
Track only. No order.
Not taken: binary lottery, AVOID_CHASE, severe extension, or a bounce-day short.
Limited-leftover short candidate from the shorts sleeve. Waits for a trigger. Not a leftover-rich EXIT.
Held, print near, move support weak or spent. Trim 30–50% before the print. Sticks while dte ≤ 7.
Hold through the print: quality entry state and move support intact. No add into extreme extension.
Drift unfinished. Hold or add into the run-up with a pre-committed sell into strength or into the print.
Starter into the event on a classified long setup (timing not AVOID_CHASE). Keep after the print only if the reaction confirms.
Short into the event on deterioration plus event risk. Invalidation above. Time stop 2–5 days after the print.
22–60d. Unpaid leftover plus a live weeks profile. Same capital as the leftover ADD, not a second event ticket.
Paid / extended into a dated print. Trim into strength (0–7d) or watch to sell the last two weeks (22–60d). Not a new short.
22–60d limited leftover plus deterioration. Candidate for a later SHORT_PRE. Not a short on a bounce tape.
Near earnings, no classified setup yet. No pre-print add.
Continuity flag: any one of the six kill rules fired (with numbers). The only path from a prior ADD/NEW to EXIT.
Operator Grade after reading support and conflicts. Not a probability.
Already-booked P&L versus cost, %, and that dollar amount as % of NAV.
$ and % NAV if the price prints the 50-day, or close − 1.5×ATR(P). Positive SMA50 means the average is above the mark (a bounce, not a stop).
Sell 33% at the mark: cash raised, and the NAV-at-risk that remains. trim25 / trim50 are the same at that size.
Same as trim33 at 25% or 50%.
Largest single-name wipe, % of NAV.
Price 10 / 20 / 25% below cost. c15 is the continuity thesis-kill rung.

stop_below: close is above the 50-day, so the 50-day is the first stop and the starter can be the mark. reclaim: the 50-day is overhead; do not buy the mark, the entry is a print through that average.
inside, above_band, or below_band at the row's own close. Above the band is not a new fill. Below waits for the 50-day.
Same read at a later close. through_kill means this entry is already dead; the band prices do not move.
Advice columns: about $5,000 for a new line, about $1,000 for an add to a held line. Not a filter and not a hard cash target.
this_entry: a print at kill_px ends this entry only. A later catalog row is a new band.
Pack/CLI field on movers leaders: IS_SUPPORTED / CHASE / UNSUPPORTED / MIXED (sleeves.classify_up_tape). First pass; the page may override with Val / Peer / Proj / Tech.
Who carries pack leftover: edge_only, both, street, or none (derive.leftover_carrier). A label, not a cutoff.
25-week change in weeks bo (bo_last - bo_first) from weeks_progression. Mesh P uses it. Not a score.
Weeks in the 25-week bo span. Mesh P needs at least 8.
Weeks early_momentum_inflection, recovery, and sustained_momentum_safety profile scores.
Weeks fragility_short and mean_reversion_exhaustion profile scores. Higher = more short-side support.
Last price in the locked all-fields / prediction tape (local currency for non-US lines).
Market capitalization, USD.
Position mark in USD; before and after the capital plan.
Whole shares. On a capital plan: floor(usd / px).
Planned fill price on the capital plan (inside the entry band).
Fraction of the line sold on a TRIM / DERISK row (EXIT is 1.0).
Capital plan: cash raised by a sell row / spent by a buy row.
Position or industry as % of NAV before and after the plan (NAV = equity mark + cash before the plan).
under_starter_hint when a NEW line is planned under about $5,000 (beyond one-share rounding). Advice, not a block.
Capital plan summary: cash at the start (USD and % NAV), cash from sells, cash to buys, cash at the end (USD and % NAV), and how many ~$5,000 starters the end cash still covers. Not a budget.
TradingView price/book and EV/free-cash-flow, trailing.
Name as % of NAV: the ceiling if the price goes to zero.
Projection forward EV/EBITDA (fp_evebitda_y1). A derivative; can be off. evebitda_fwd_peer bins it versus the industry median.
Horizon 0-7 sessions: a trade on the tape, a print or a trigger.
Horizon 8-60 sessions: a position built on leftover, weeks bo and the entry band.
A hold beyond 60 sessions, or a held line that is not a NEW slot.

Five lens percentiles in order G E M P V, each 0-99 in today's GMV universe (NASDAQ / NYSE / AMEX, market cap at least $1B). G growth, E estimates, M momentum, P participation (volume), V value. Each lens is the median percentile of its own parts; -- means fewer than two parts were present. Lenses are never added together.
The profile that brought the name into Focus: its first place in the round-robin (rank 1 of every long profile, then rank 2, and so on).
Every long profile (COMPOUNDER, RERATE, BREAKOUT, VALUE_TURN, ALL5) the name ranked in after the industry cap, comma-separated.
The GMV profile this row belongs to.
The profile's weakest lens percentile (0-1) for this name. The profile sorts on it, ties on the mean of the same lenses. For FADE it is the weakest of 1 - M, 1 - E and 1 - P.
Letter of the name's lowest lens percentile (G, E, M, P or V).
Letter of the name's highest lens percentile.
Label from trend_q, r_1m and hi_prox (bands in config/generic_utils/gmv_lens.json). Not a rank.
tape_state: trend_q at least 0.35, not PULLBACK or EXTENDED.
tape_state: trend_q at least 0.35 and r_1m at most -4%. An uptrend that is giving back this month.
tape_state: trend_q at least 0.35, hi_prox at least -2% (at or near the 91-day high) and r_1m at least 15%.
tape_state: trend_q between -0.35 and 0.35. No clear trend.
tape_state: trend_q at most -0.35.
tape_state: fewer than 20 snapshots in the 91-day window, so no trend fit.
Profile, mid term: weakest of G, E and M. Growth that estimates and the tape both confirm. Value is shown, not used.
Profile, mid term: weakest of G, E and V. Growth with rising estimates that still trades cheap to peers. Momentum is not used, so many are early or still falling.
Profile, short term: weakest of M, P and E. Trend with volume behind it and estimates moving up. A trade, not a valuation call.
Profile, short to mid term: weakest of V, E and P. Cheap names where estimates turn up and buyers come back. The rebound case with evidence.
Profile, mid term: weakest of all five lenses. No weak lens.
Profile, short term, inverted: weakest of 1 - M, 1 - E and 1 - P. Weak trend, falling estimates and sellers in control together. Short candidates, not an automatic short.
Close versus the snapshot about 30 calendar days earlier, %. Split-adjusted all-fields snapshots.
Close versus the snapshot about 91 calendar days earlier, %.
Signed R squared of ln(close) on calendar day over the last 91 days: the sign of the slope times R squared. +1 is a straight rising line, -1 a straight falling one, near 0 no trend.
Annualized slope of the trend_q fit, %.
r_3m divided by (vol_d x square root of 63): the 3-month return in units of the name's own daily volatility. The only place volatility enters a lens, as a denominator.
Close versus the highest close of the last 91 days, %. 0 is at the high.

Last 30 days: summed relative volume on up days divided by summed relative volume on down days (day change field). Above 1 is heavier volume on up days. Relative volume is read at scan time, so intraday snapshots add noise.
Last 91 days: sum of sign(day change) x relative volume, divided by summed relative volume. -1 to 1; positive is accumulation.
10-day average volume versus 30-day average volume, %.
Standard deviation of the daily change field over 91 days, %. Size, not quality. Never a lens of its own.
ATRP x square root of 20, %. Size of a typical 20-day move. Not a direction.
Street revenue forecast for the next fiscal year versus trailing 12-month revenue, %.
Street EPS forecast for the next fiscal year versus trailing diluted EPS, %. Blank when either is at or under 0.
Trailing 12-month revenue growth year over year, %.
Trailing diluted EPS growth year over year, %.
Compounded change of the next-FY EPS forecast across snapshots over about 91 days, %. A single step beyond 25% is skipped as a fiscal-year roll.
Next-FY EPS forecast, same window: (up steps - down steps) divided by steps that moved. -1 to 1.
Compounded change of the next-FY revenue forecast over about 91 days, %. Same roll rule as eps_rev_3m.
Average price target now versus about 91 days ago, %.
Last reported quarter's EPS surprise, % (eps_surprise_percent_fq).
Close divided by the street next-FY EPS forecast. Not pe_fwd, which is the projection PE.
pe_nfy divided by fwd_eps_g. Lower is cheaper growth. Blank when growth is at or under 0.
Average price target versus close, %, from today's all-fields scan. The pack's street_left is the same idea from the pack tape; it is an overlay here, not a lens part.
Evidence row type: part (one metric), lens (G E M P V), or profile.
Calendar days from the evaluation snapshot to the later close the rank is compared with.
Evaluation days with a usable rank correlation.
Mean Spearman rank correlation between the ordering and the later return across evaluation days. Positive means a higher place led a higher return.
ic_mean divided by its standard deviation, times the square root of n_days. A size check: horizons overlap, so it is not a significance test.
Share of evaluation days with a positive rank correlation.
Mean rank correlation of the last three evaluation days. Shows a lens that changed sign inside the window.
Rank correlation on the last evaluation day.
Mean later return of the top 20% by that ordering minus the universe mean, percentage points, averaged across days.
First evaluation day.
Last evaluation day (the latest day with the full horizon ahead).
Growth parts left empty because the print was beyond 300% (growth_quote_max_pct): a tiny prior-year base, not a rate to rank. Same rule as the growth radar.
Industry median of pe_nfy (close / street next-FY EPS) in the same day's GMV universe ($1B+, at least 6 names).
Lowest forward PE (close / next-FY EPS forecast) the name traded at across the history window (about 7 months of day files).
Median forward PE across the history window.
Highest forward PE across the history window.
Where today's forward PE sits in its window range, 0-100: 0 is the cheapest multiple of the window, 100 the richest.
Today's next-FY EPS forecast x pe_nfy_min: the price if the market paid the window's cheapest multiple.
px_own_low_pe versus the close, %. Near 0 means the price already sits on the window's cheapest multiple.
Today's next-FY EPS forecast x pe_nfy_med: the price at the name's own median multiple.
px_own_med_pe versus the close, %. Positive is room back to the name's own median multiple.
Today's next-FY EPS forecast x pe_nfy_ind_med: the price at the industry median multiple.
px_peer_pe versus the close, %. Positive is a discount to peers on forward earnings.
Highest split-adjusted close in the history window.
Day of window_high.
Lowest split-adjusted close in the history window. The support the buy-in-red band anchors on.
Day of window_low.
Close versus window_high, %.
Close versus window_low, %.
Next-FY EPS forecast now versus the first day of the window, %, split-adjusted. A fiscal-year roll can lift it in one step.
Average price target now versus the first day of the window, %, split-adjusted.
Forward PE now versus the first day of the window, %. Negative: the price fell behind the estimate (de-rating); positive: the multiple expanded (re-rating).
Split-like jumps rescaled in the window (split guard: consecutive snapshots at most 5 days apart, a close ratio of 1.8 or more, and a day change under 25%).
Top of the buy-in-red band: close - 0.5 ATR. A fill on a red day, not at the mark.
Bottom of the buy-in-red band: close - 1.5 ATR, or the window low when it sits inside the band.
atr: the band is ATR multiples under the close. window_low: the band's low is the window low. +support_kill: the kill sits under the window low (support within 1 ATR under the band).
Price that ends a buy-in-red entry: 0.75 ATR under the band low (or under the window low when that support is just below). Not the entry book's kill_px.
bounce_kill versus the close, %.
First target of a bounce entry: the 50-day average when it is above the band, else the street target.
sma50 or street_px: which price first_target is.
(first_target - bounce_high) / (bounce_high - bounce_kill). A ratio, not a 0-100.
Low of the entry book's 50-day reclaim band. A close back inside it is the confirmation add.
High of the entry book's 50-day reclaim band.
Lower of the street target and window_high, when it is above the close. Where a held line lightens.
open: trim_zone is above the close. above_street: the close is already at or over the street target, so a held line is in its trim zone now.
Today's next-FY EPS forecast (close / pe_nfy).
Split-adjusted close now versus the first day of the history window, %.

Balance-sheet label (discount path): net_cash = net debt at or under 0; levered = net debt / EBITDA at least 4; covered = net debt / EBITDA at most 2 with operating margin at least 8% and FCF not negative; open = none of those; thin = no debt and no EBITDA field. A label, not a rank.
Cash divided by total debt. Above 1 is more cash than debt.
Net debt divided by trailing EBITDA (empty when EBITDA is at or under 0). Negative is net cash.
How many of the name's multiple paths (PE, EV/Rev, EV/EBITDA, P/B, EV/FCF) are CHEAPER over the history window. A count, not a 0-100.
Trailing PE path over the window: CHEAPER (change at most -5%), RICHER (at least +5%), FLAT (between), THIN_HIST (fewer than 4 prints). pe_pct beside it is the change.
EV/EBITDA path over the window, same rule as pe_path; evebitda_pct is the change.
EV/FCF path over the window, same rule as pe_path; evfcf_pct is the change.
The largest gap to an industry median among the name's multiples, %. The widest single discount, not a sum.
Number of day prints behind the multiple paths.
A multiple path that changed between -5% and +5% over the window.
A multiple path that rose at least 5% over the window: the market pays more per unit of earnings than at the start.
First weekly run in the span (weeks_progression).
Last weekly run in the span.
Weeks bo at the start of the span.
Weeks bo at the end of the span.
Lowest weeks bo in the span.
Highest weeks bo in the span.
Weeks cont at the start of the span.
Weeks cont at the end of the span.
cont_last minus cont_first.
Weeks fwd at the start of the span.
Weeks fwd at the end of the span.
fwd_last minus fwd_first.
Latest weekly early score.
Latest weekly recovery score.
Latest weekly fragility score.
Latest weekly exhaustion score.
Week (or day) the row describes.
Which list a breadth row averages (the playbook sleeve).
Price at the early all-fields run of the day (run_a).
Price at the later run (run_b).
The scan's day change at the early run, %.
The scan's day change at the later run, %.
close_b versus close_a, %: how the name moved between the two runs.
Relative volume (10-day) at the early run; intraday values are partial-day.
Relative volume (10-day) at the later run; intraday values are partial-day.
EXTENDING, FADING, REVERSING_UP, REVERSING_DOWN or FLAT, from the sign of the early day change and the later drift.
session_path: the later run adds to the early move (up and up, or down and down).
session_path: the later run gives some of the early move back without flipping the day's sign.
session_path: red at the early run, green by the later run.
session_path: green at the early run, red by the later run.
Industry median of change_a.
Industry median of change_b.
Industry median of drift_pct.
Share of the industry's names with drift_pct above 0, %.
COMPOUNDER floor: the weakest of G, E and M for this name (0-1). That profile sorts on it.
